original_question: Let nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1) and let u(n) be the maximum of nu_w over w in S_n. For each n, characterize the permutations that attain u(n), and determine whether these maximizing permutations have a limiting shape as n tends to infinity.
target_in_paper: Section 2 (Problems of 2025), Problem 12 of On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems. The nearby Problem 13 gives the paper's intended conjectural sharpening: the maximizers should be Richardson/layered permutations.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact core of Problem 12: it fixes nu_w as the principal specialization S_w(1, ..., 1), defines u(n) as the maximum over w in S_n, asks for the maximizing permutations for each n, and asks for an asymptotic 'limiting shape' of those maximizers. It also stays correctly separate from Problem 11, which is the different question about the exponential growth rate of u(n).
missing_details: Specify that S_w is the type-A Schubert polynomial attached to a permutation w in S_n, usually viewed in Z[x_1, x_2, ...] (or equivalently in finitely many variables for fixed n).
State explicitly that nu_w = S_w(1, 1, ...) is the principal specialization, i.e. the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial.
Quantify over every integer n >= 1 and make clear that one is asking for the full maximizing set M_n = {w in S_n : nu_w = u(n)}, since the maximizer need not be unique.
Make precise what object is supposed to have a 'limiting shape'; the natural stand-alone interpretation is the rescaled permutation plot or permutation matrix in the unit square.
Include the paper-faithful nearby conjectural refinement from Problem 13: the expected maximizing permutations are Richardson/layered permutations of the explicit block-decreasing form.
No extra hypotheses on characteristic, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency are part of this problem; the only algebraic setting needed is ordinary Schubert polynomials and their principal evaluations.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group and, for w in S_n, let Sch_w denote the type-A Schubert polynomial of w. Define nu_w := Sch_w(1,1,...) (equivalently, the sum of the coefficients of Sch_w), and set u(n) := max_{w in S_n} nu_w. Determine the full maximizing set M_n := {w in S_n : nu_w = u(n)}. In particular, decide whether every maximizer is a Richardson/layered permutation of the form (i_1, i_1-1, ..., 2, 1, i_2, i_2-1, ..., i_1+1, i_3, ..., i_2+1, ...) for some i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k = n. As n -> infinity, do the maximizers in M_n admit a limiting description or limit shape under the standard rescaling of their permutation plots (equivalently, permutation matrices) to [0,1]^2, and if so, what is it?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Problem 12 in the notebook, so that is the correct target. I did not replace it by Problem 13, because Problem 13 is a stronger nearby conjectural answer rather than the open question itself. To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, I made explicit the Schubert-polynomial setting, the meaning of principal specialization, the fact that one should classify all maximizers for each n, and the natural geometric carrier of a possible limit shape. I also folded in the Richardson/layered class only as the paper's nearby intended characterization, not as a replacement of the target question. This matches the way the notebook organizes the topic: Problem 11 asks about the asymptotic size of u(n), Problem 12 asks for the maximizers and their limiting shape, and Problem 13 proposes the Richardson/layered conjecture as the likely answer.
